app.title: Nanoindentation explorer (nanoDMA depth-profile explorer)
app.summary: A person uploads many instrument text exports. The app reads the sample, fluence, grain and replicate number from each file name. They tick which measurements to show, filter by sample, fluence, grain or group, and can put the shown files into named custom groups, each listed in its own tab. They choose a quantity, a depth binning and a plot mode. The plot then overlays each indent's depth profile, or shows one centre curve per group with a std or SEM band. They leave with a ZIP of the plotted curves as CSVs and a CSV of per-measurement means, plus a table of averages per grain.

task.text: Compare depth profiles of mechanical properties across replicate indents and across groups of measurements, and export the binned and averaged curves.

data.text: Many tab-separated instrument exports. Each holds thousands of rows of storage modulus, hardness and contact depth over one indent, with sample, fluence, grain and replicate encoded in the file name.
data.item: one indent measurement: a file holding a depth profile of storage modulus, hardness and contact depth

stage.text: exploring and comparing indentation depth profiles across grains and conditions, after measurement

mechanism.text: Sidebar controls set the quantity, axis, plot mode and bin count. Data editors in tabs (one for ungrouped files, one per custom group) set which files are drawn and how they are grouped. The plot redraws from those choices as overlaid binned curves or as group centre lines with spread bands, and a summary table below gives per-file and per-grain means. Both can be downloaded as CSV.

field.text: nanoindentation depth profiles (nanoDMA) in materials science

workflow.name: overlay and average replicate curves by group, then export them

steps.here: Drag in many *_DYN.txt exports. Each file's header row is found and mapped to canonical columns, and its file name is decoded into sample, fluence, grain and measurement. Files that cannot be parsed are listed in the sidebar.

steps.step: filter to the items that matter
steps.here: Multiselects for sample, fluence, grain and group narrow the list, and a Show checkbox on each row picks which indents are drawn
Type a group name and press 'Add shown to group' to move the ticked files into a named group with its own tab. Groups can be disbanded or cleared.

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: Each profile is binned over contact depth (20–400 bins). In the per-group modes, the replicates are combined bin by bin as mean or median ± std or SEM, grouped by grain or by custom group.
Per-indent curves are overlaid, coloured by grain, fluence, measurement or file, or the group centre curves are overlaid with shaded spread bands and hover values
A table gives each measurement's mean storage modulus, hardness and contact depth, and an expander averages them per fluence and grain
A ZIP of one CSV per plotted curve, exactly as binned and shown, and a CSV of the per-measurement summary

distinctive: Experimental factors (sample, fluence, grain, replicate) are decoded from a fixed file-naming convention rather than entered by hand
Replicates are binned onto shared depth edges before averaging. Each bin keeps its replicate count n, so SEM can be shown as std/√n.
There is a choice between a mean and a median centre, and between a std and an SEM band, to be robust to outlier indents
Custom groups that cut across the decoded metadata can be built from whatever is currently ticked and compared as averaged curves
The exported curves are exactly what is drawn, after depth binning, not the roughly 17k raw points per file
